headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because ctx writes filesystem/MCP context while kotaemon handles documents and API keys with broad network egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code events and uses filesystem/MCP surfaces, while kotaemon ingests documents/HTML/PDFs that may contain attacker-controlled instructions. If kotaemon output is copied into ctx-managed context or files, prompt injection can cross the pair. The pathway is plausible in default workflows, though not proven directly.
conditions: IF kotaemon outputs are pasted into ctx-managed files or MCP context
IF ctx treats file or event content as trusted instructions
mitigations: Add a manual review step before ctx ingests kotaemon-generated text
Restrict ctx to allowlisted file paths only
Strip instructions from imported documents before indexing
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between document ingestion and context management

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches filesystem, audit/runtime logs, graph data, and MCP servers; kotaemon handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys, and can send content to external APIs with broad egress. If they share a workspace or files, sensitive material from kotaemon can be exposed through ctx logs or downstream API calls. The blast radius includes secrets and documents.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace or ./ktem_app_data-equivalent files
IF kotaemon sends shared documents or transcripts to a third-party API
mitigations: Separate the agents into different OS users
Move secrets out of shared directories
Disable external API providers for sensitive corpora
Rotate any API keys exposed in shared logs
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and per-agent encryption

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, and ctx writes filesystem/MCP state while kotaemon writes ./ktem_app_data and uses elevated Docker privileges. Overlapping writes to shared directories or mutable project state can race and corrupt outputs. This is not proven to be default, but the write surfaces make conflict plausible.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF either agent mutates shared git or config state without locking
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories
Run only one writer per repository at a time
Use file locks around shared state
Snapshot data before batch runs
requires-engineering: add transactional writes or locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx is designed to observe tool events and manage context, while kotaemon produces document-grounded answers from PDFs, HTML, and citations. If ctx forwards kotaemon output into later actions without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream work. The pair does not guarantee verification, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF ctx uses kotaemon output as authoritative context
IF downstream automation acts on kotaemon citations without human review
mitigations: Require human approval before acting on generated facts
Cross-check citations against source documents
Limit ctx to summarizing rather than executing kotaemon outputs
Log provenance for every forwarded claim
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and broad document classes, while ctx records audit/runtime logs and harness records. If regulated or secret-bearing documents flow through both, retention and residency controls may diverge, creating a compliance mismatch. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction, so this is a general but credible mismatch rather than a higher-severity residency finding.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are processed by kotaemon
IF ctx retains logs longer than the source-data retention policy
mitigations: Classify data before ingestion
Exclude secrets from logs
Set short retention on audit/runtime logs
Document which APIs receive which data classes
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls across both systems
